title: Per-extension state persistence (design only, gated on WI-8 and WI-9)
one_line: Write one design document that decides where a plugin's own key-value state lives, and do not build it — because the cleanup half of the answer is not implementable until WI-9 gives extensions a real unload, and a store built before that has to have a lifecycle bolted onto it later, which costs more than designing one with a lifecycle now.
user_visible_effect: None. This item ships a document. The visible effect is that a plugin author asking "where do I put my state, and will you clean it up when I uninstall?" gets one answer with a stated path, a stated lifecycle, and a stated reason the other two candidate substrates were rejected — instead of a `docs/extensions.md` recipe that says "append a custom session entry and rebuild it from the branch," which is session-scoped and therefore cannot be the answer for anything that must survive a session. The second visible effect is that the decision to DEFER the build stops being invisible: the document names the unowned work item, its technical precondition (WI-9), and the two contracts a future implementer must defend.
effort: S for the design, matching the plan's 'S mỗi cái' rating for wave 8. Half a day of research plus a day of writing is the realistic number, not four hours, because step 2 (auditing what an extension can do today) is research the plan never did and it changes what the document has to say. The build is M and is NOT in this item and NOT in M2. Be aware the plan's own wave table calls wave 8 'S mỗi cái, không build' while §8.2 says the build is unowned and must be named and dated before M2 closes — those are consistent only if you read 'S' as covering the document alone, which is how this spec reads it.
risk: Building it before WI-9 — the plan names this correctly and it is the whole risk. The signature is a `state` handle appearing on ExtensionContext with a JSON file behind it and no owner: at that point WI-9 has to retrofit a lifecycle onto a store that already has callers, and retrofitting ownership onto a store that already has callers is materially more expensive than designing one with ownership from the start, because every existing call site becomes a call site that can now be cleaned out from under itself. The second failure is a document that picks a substrate and does not say why the other two were rejected — a decision without a rejection reads as an oversight, and the next person reopens it. The third, and specific to this tree, is writing the document against the two substrates the plan names and missing the third one that already ships and is already documented: `docs/extensions.md:699-723` tells authors to persist durable state with `pi.appendEntry("com.example.my-extension.state", data)` and rebuild it from `ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()`. That is session-scoped — it dies with the session, and it is a reconstruction pattern, not a key-value store. A design doc that never mentions it will be read as having surveyed the options when it did not.

steps.instruction: BEFORE writing anything, re-read the prohibition in gate step 1 and accept it: this item may not touch a single `.ts` file. The plan is explicit — 'Không build, không test dưới M2' — and the temptation is concrete, because the two future contracts in step 6 read like test cases and it is one edit away from becoming code. If you find yourself writing a test, stop: AGENTS.md bans placeholder tests and the plan's own reasoning says a test here 'sẽ cho ra đúng một placeholder mà AGENTS.md cấm'.

Write the survey FIRST, before the recommendation, because the survey is what makes the recommendation checkable and it is the part the plan never did. The plan asserts as status quo that 'một extension cần nhớ bất cứ thứ gì sẽ tự chế file dưới `~/.omp` hoặc `cwd`' — DO NOT write that as observed fact, because it is not. `grep -nE 'Bun.write|Bun.file|readFileSync|writeFileSync' packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/*.ts` returns ZERO hits; no in-repo example extension persists anything. What is verified is the ABSENCE of a primitive (`ExtensionAPI` has 69 methods at `types.ts:1256-1582` and none of them is a store), plus one documented workaround (step 3). Write the honest version: there is no store, so third-party extensions have no sanctioned place to put state, and the DIY-file pattern is a predictable consequence rather than something this repo has been observed doing. Getting this wrong in the direction of overstating is the failure the plan itself warns about five lines later.

Read this section and quote it in the survey. It is the substrate that already ships and the only one an author can reach today: `pi.appendEntry("com.example.my-extension.state", data)` (signature at `types.ts:1489`) plus a rebuild from `ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()` on `session_start` / `session_branch` / `session_tree`. State plainly why it is not the answer to this design question — custom entries live on a session branch, so they do not survive the session, and the pattern is append-and-replay (latest matching entry wins) rather than a keyed get/set. Do NOT delete or rewrite this section in this item: the pattern is still the correct advice for session-scoped state, and the design doc is a forward-looking decision about a store that does not exist yet. The only edit to `docs/extensions.md` this item makes is a cross-link (step 8).

State the design question in one sentence and then answer it: does an extension get a namespaced key-value store INSIDE the existing layered `Settings`, or a dedicated per-extension store with its own lifecycle and unload cleanup? Rank all THREE substrates from step 2/3 (A Settings overlay, B dedicated store, C session-entry replay) and RECOMMEND B. For each rejected one, write the specific reason, not a category: A is rejected because plugin-internal state is not user configuration and would live in a YAML file users hand-edit, and because the six `SettingProvenance` layers (`config/settings.ts:62`) name USER intent and do not describe where plugin cache state came from; C is rejected because it is session-scoped and is append-and-replay, not keyed get/set. A recommendation without named rejections is the failure mode — it reads as an oversight and the next person reopens the question.

Include the code_shape sketch above, marked unmistakably as a sketch, and say the load-bearing thing in prose: ownership is per-extension IDENTITY (the install path), not per `ExtensionContext`, because `ExtensionContext` is rebuilt on every invocation and a handle hung off it would be per-call. Key the host map the way `extension.flags` is keyed at `loader.ts:263` — by `extensionPath` — and say explicitly that it must NOT be keyed the way `runtime.flagValues` is at `loader.ts:265`, which is keyed by bare flag name and is the shape WI-9 exists to change. Then NAME a concrete on-disk path and justify it (`~/.omp/extensions-state/<extension-id>.json` follows the existing `getPluginsDir()` conventions; the helper belongs in `packages/utils/src/dirs.ts` next to `getPluginsLockfile` at `:652-654`). A doc that says 'the path will be decided later' has deferred the decision instead of making it and fails acceptance.

steps.anchor: docs/extension-state-persistence.md §'Contracts a future build must defend'
steps.instruction: Write down BOTH writable contracts now, in the present tense, as things a future implementer must defend — not as tests, not as TODO code. (1) An extension's state is dropped when that extension is unloaded, and dropping one extension's state leaves every other extension's state readable even when two extensions claimed the same key name. (2) An extension that changes its id or install path does not silently orphan its previous values — the doc must say what happens to them (refuse the rename, migrate them, or document them as abandoned), because 'a renamed setting does not orphan a value' is unanswerable until the rename case is stated. Reuse WI-9's ownership contract verbatim where it already exists (plan §11.3) rather than inventing a parallel one; two subtly different ownership contracts in one milestone is a future bug.

Close with the deferral, stated so it cannot be read as settled. Name the build as an UNOWNED work item, name its technical precondition (WI-9, wave 7 — 'cleanup on uninstall is not implementable without a real unload'), and record that no milestone in the plan claims it. The plan (§8.2) requires this decision to be named and dated before M2 closes, and requires that it NOT be written as 'Phase 4/5' because the plan has no phase concept. If the doc cannot say plainly 'this is designed, not built, and nobody owns the build', it has not finished. Consider also recording, in one line, that if the build IS pulled into M2 after wave 7, WI-9 being green is a NECESSARY condition and not a SUFFICIENT one — the plan says this explicitly and it is the sentence most likely to be lost.

Add ONE short paragraph at the top of '## Session and state patterns' that points at docs/extension-state-persistence.md and states the status honestly: there is no dedicated per-extension state store today; the substrate question has been decided in that document; the build is deferred and unowned. Do not rewrite the existing `appendEntry` guidance and do not present the decision as shipped — an author reading this page must not conclude that `pi.state` exists. Keep it to the point where an author can tell in five seconds whether this changes what they should do today (it does not).

DECISION REQUIRED, see open_questions: this spec's default is to add NO changelog entry, because nothing user-visible changes and AGENTS.md scopes changelog entries to 'user-facing: lead with what the user will see or can now do'. The sibling WI-0 spec chose to add one, so if the maintainer wants wave-8 consistency, add exactly one line under `## [Unreleased]` reading roughly 'Documented the design for per-extension state persistence; the store itself is deferred pending extension unload' — and touch nothing else in the file. If the maintainer agrees with this spec's default, skip the file entirely. Do not half-do it: an entry that implies a feature exists is worse than no entry.

verification:
Human review of the design document, by ONE maintainer. There is NO build gate and NO test gate, and the plan is right about why — nothing in the tree changes behaviour, so `bun run check:ts` is entirely unaffected by this item and presenting it as evidence for WI-11 is the fastest way to make a design item look finished when it is not.

ENVIRONMENT, verified first-hand at HEAD 808b365 on branch milestone-1: `bun run check:ts` is GREEN (all 14 packages report Done; pi-coding-agent:check:types Done in 10.18s) — so a red typecheck after your change means you broke something, though for this item it should be impossible. `bun test` is BLOCKED: running `bun test test/extension-context-project-trust.test.ts` from packages/coding-agent reports '0 pass, 1 fail, 1 error' with 'Failed to load pi_natives native addon for darwin-arm64'. Build the addon with `bun --cwd=packages/natives run build` before any item that needs a real test run; WI-11 does not.

Commands that must hold after the change (run from repo root):

1. `git diff --name-only | grep -c '\.ts$'` returns 0. This is the load-bearing check of the whole item: any non-zero value means code was written, which the plan forbids in as many words ('Cấm bắt đầu bằng code' is WI-0's phrasing, WI-11's is 'Không build, không test dưới M2').
2. `git status --porcelain` shows exactly the files in files_touched and nothing else — no stray scratch files, no edits to COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_OMP_UPGRADE.md.
3. `grep -n -iE 'Settings|dedicated|substrate' docs/extension-state-persistence.md` returns hits for all THREE ranked options, proving the survey happened before the recommendation.
4. `grep -n 'appendEntry' docs/extension-state-persistence.md` returns a hit — the already-shipping substrate is named, not skipped.
5. `grep -n -iE 'unload|WI-9' docs/extension-state-persistence.md` returns hits — the technical precondition is named.
6. `grep -n -iE 'unowned|deferred|không ai nhận|not owned' docs/extension-state-persistence.md` returns a hit — the deferral is recorded, not implied.
7. `grep -n 'extensions-state' docs/extension-state-persistence.md` returns a hit — a concrete on-disk path was chosen, not deferred.
8. The maintainer opens docs/extension-state-persistence.md and answers, from the text alone and without asking the author: (a) which substrate won, and why were the other two rejected; (b) where does the data live on disk; (c) what happens to an extension's state when it is unloaded; (d) what happens to its values when it is renamed; (e) who owns the build and what gates it. Any unanswered question fails the item.
9. The maintainer confirms the document does NOT read as shipped: reading it must not lead anyone to believe `pi.state` or an `ExtensionContext.state` member exists today.
gate:
DONE means all six of the following hold.

(1) `git diff --name-only | grep -c '\.ts$'` returns 0. Zero TypeScript files touched. A design item that ships an edit to `types.ts` has failed regardless of what the prose says.

(2) `docs/extension-state-persistence.md` exists, and it RANKED three substrates and recommended one. Grep step 3 and 4 above must produce hits. The failure this prevents is a document that names a winner without naming what it beat, which reads as an oversight rather than a decision.

(3) The document names a concrete on-disk path (grep step 7) and a concrete ownership unit — per extension identity, keyed by install path, matching `extension.flags` at `loader.ts:263` and explicitly NOT `runtime.flagValues` at `loader.ts:265`. A document that says the path will be decided later has deferred the decision instead of making it.

(4) Both future contracts are written down in the present tense (step 6), and the second one states what happens to values on rename rather than only asserting that a rename must not orphan them. An unstated rename policy is the whole hole a reader will fall into.

(5) The deferral is recorded: the build is named as unowned, WI-9 is named as its technical precondition, and the text does NOT use the phrase 'Phase 4/5' or any other phase label (the plan has no phase concept and explicitly forbids writing one). Additionally: if the text mentions pulling the build into M2, it must state that green WI-9 is necessary and not sufficient.

(6) The maintainer answers all five questions in verification step 8 from the document's text alone. This is the human-review gate the plan asks for ('Review người tài liệu thiết kế') and the ONLY gate — there is no automated substitute and pretending otherwise is how this item gets closed while producing prose nobody checked.

Note what is NOT part of the gate: `bun run check:ts` passing proves nothing about this item and must not be cited as evidence; no test may be added, because the plan's stated reason is that cleanup-on-uninstall is not implementable until WI-9 lands, so a test written now would be exactly the placeholder AGENTS.md forbids.
test_contract:
There is NO test, and that is the correct instrument rather than a gap. The plan's reason is substantive, not procedural: cleanup on uninstall is not implementable until WI-9 provides a real unload, so any test written today would assert against a store that does not exist and against a lifecycle nobody has built — the exact placeholder AGENTS.md bans. Writing one would also be actively harmful, because a passing test for a deferred feature is indistinguishable from a passing test for a shipped one to anyone reading CI later.

The contract is a FIVE-QUESTION acceptance a maintainer must answer from the document's text alone, without asking the author: (a) which substrate won, and specifically why each of the other two was rejected; (b) where does the data live on disk; (c) what happens to an extension's state when it is unloaded, and does unloading one extension leave another's values readable; (d) what happens to an extension's values when it is renamed or moves install path; (e) who owns the build and what gates it. Any question the document cannot answer means the document is not finished.

Two NEGATIVE contracts also hold and must not be violated. First, the document must not read as shipped — nobody reading it may conclude that a `state` member exists on `ExtensionContext` today. Second, the document must not use a phase label; the plan has no phase concept and writing 'Phase 4/5' invents structure that does not exist.

What a consumer sees if this regresses: the substrate question stays open, so the first person to need per-extension state builds whichever store is convenient — very likely the DIY file under `~/.omp` or `cwd` the plan describes as the predictable failure — and that store ships with no owner and no cleanup path. By the time WI-9 lands and wants to clean up what an extension wrote, the store has callers and retrofitting ownership onto a live store is materially more expensive than the design that would have made it a one-line unload arm. The cost is not the code; it is that a decision nobody wrote down gets made by whoever needed a feature first, and changing it later is a breaking change for every extension author who shipped against it.
test_files: NONE WRITTEN BY THIS ITEM. No test file is created, and none may be. The plan states the reason directly: 'Không dưới M2 — đây là mục thiết kế và cố ý ngoài phạm vi build, vì cleanup khi uninstall không thi triển khả thi tới khi WI-9 có một unload thật. Viết test bây giờ sẽ cho ra đúng một placeholder mà AGENTS.md cấm.'

packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/types.ts:452-562 — the `ExtensionContext` interface this item is ABOUT and must NOT modify. Cited by inspection as the thing a build would add one member to (`state`). It currently declares 26 unique members (27 declarations; `isProjectTrusted(): boolean` is declared twice, at :494 and :561). The plan's '12 field' figure is wrong — see plan_corrections.

packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/loader.ts:263-265 — the precedent the ownership shape must follow. `:263` sets `extension.flags` WITH `extensionPath: this.extension.path`; `:265` sets `runtime.flagValues` WITHOUT it, keyed by bare flag name. Plan §11.3 records that the flagValues shape is what WI-9 changes. A future state store must be keyed the way `:263` is, not the way `:265` is.

packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/types.ts:1256-1582 — `ExtensionAPI`, the surface the plan says has no storage primitive. VERIFIED by enumeration: 80 members, 69 of them methods, none a store. The plan's '29 phương thức' is wrong by a factor of 2.4 — see plan_corrections.

packages/coding-agent/src/memory-backend/types.ts:79-83 — `MemoryRuntimeContext`, the three-method (`status`/`search`/`save`) content-memory surface exposed as `ExtensionContext.memory` at `types.ts:506`. Cited because the design doc must say why it is NOT the answer: it is agent content memory, not a per-extension keyed store, and a doc that skips this will be asked about it.

docs/extensions.md:699-723 — the already-shipping 'Session and state patterns' section. Not a test and not modified beyond one cross-link paragraph; cited because it is the third substrate and the only one reachable today, and the design doc is invalid without it.

Do NOT rewrite or delete the existing `appendEntry` guidance at :701-722 — it remains correct advice for session-scoped state.

depends_on: WI-8 (specifically WI-8a's substrate decision, Option A) — soft dependency, resolvable now. WI-8a routes plugin SETTINGS through `Settings` as a namespaced overlay. WI-11 asks the same substrate question about plugin STATE and the plan's whole point is that the two have DIFFERENT answers. This dependency is soft because the WI-11 document is required to argue that difference explicitly, and it can be written before WI-8a lands — but if WI-8a has already landed, read `manager.ts:929-960` first, because that code is the concrete precedent for what 'the wrong substrate' looks like and the document is much stronger citing real migrated code than predicting it.

WI-9 (wave 7) — HARD dependency for the BUILD, none for the DESIGN. The plan's whole argument is that cleanup-on-uninstall is not implementable without a real unload, and this was VERIFIED: `git grep -n 'async unload|unloadExtension|#unload' -- packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/` returns ZERO hits. The only unregister seam in the entire extension API is `unregisterProvider` (`types.ts:1578`) — a single narrow provider unregistration, not a general teardown. The design document can and must be written now; the build cannot start until WI-9 lands.

WI-0 / WI-10 (wave 1) — soft, ordering only. The plan's wave table has wave 1 (trust model, canonical authoring surface) strictly before wave 8 because M2-OQ2 (does the capability registry ever become extension-reachable) changes what 'canonical' MEANS for a third-party author, and a per-extension store is a canonical authoring surface. If wave 1 has not landed, the design doc must flag that its recommendation is conditional on the trust posture and must not be written as if `ctx.state` would have a settled trust level.
blocks: The unowned build of a per-extension state store — which the plan (§8.2) requires be NAMED and DATED before M2 closes, and which no milestone currently claims. The plan's own words: 'Có kéo build này vào M2 hay không, ai làm, ở milestone nào — cả ba đều chưa được gán'. This design document is what makes that name-and-date obligation concrete.

WI-9 (wave 7) — only weakly, and only as a constraint, not a blocker. WI-9's unload arm has to know what to clean, and the store does not exist yet, so WI-9 can proceed without this item. The dependency is one-directional: this item's BUILD needs WI-9, not the other way round. Do not let this be read as a reason to reorder wave 7.

M3 (per plan §11.3: 'M3 cần: một bề mặt authoring đã chốt ... và một `unload` thật để cài/gỡ không rò'). A decided substrate is a precondition for M3 authoring surfaces; an undecided one means M3 rediscovers the question with less context than this item has.

M4 (per plan §11.3: ownership that can be verified — every registration traceable to an extension, every run-lifetime resource owned and released on teardown). A state store with no owner is a direct M4 violation, which is why the ownership unit in step 5 is not optional detail.
open_questions: CHANGELOG — does a design-only wave-8 item get a changelog entry? The sibling WI-0 spec added one; this spec's default is not to. The substance differs: WI-0's trust model constrains what third-party authors may rely on TODAY, while WI-11's design doc governs a primitive that does not exist, so no author is being held to anything by it. A maintainer should decide once for both and apply it to WI-0 and WI-12 as well. Default if undecided: no entry, per AGENTS.md's 'user-facing' scoping.

ON-DISK PATH — `~/.omp/extensions-state/<extension-id>.json` is the shape this spec proposes, following the existing `getPluginsDir()` conventions and sitting alongside `getPluginsLockfile` (`packages/utils/src/dirs.ts:652-654`). A maintainer may want a different home (inside the extension's own directory, or one file per extension with a shared index). What is NOT acceptable is leaving the path undecided — that converts a design item into a deferral wearing a design item's clothes.

M2-OQ2 — the plan's own §10 says M2-OQ2 (does the capability registry ever become extension-reachable: YES / NO / DEFERRED) blocks 'substrate của WI-11/WI-12'. If M2-OQ2 is still open when this document is written, the document must state that its recommendation is conditional on the answer rather than silently assuming one. If M2-OQ2 is closed, cite the answer and say whether it changes the recommendation.

SCOPE OF 'RENAME' — the plan's second future contract is 'một setting được đổi tên không làm mồ côi một giá trị' (a renamed setting does not orphan a value). For a state store, keys are chosen by the extension, so the interesting case is the extension's OWN identity changing (id, or install path when the user moves it), not a key rename. A maintainer must decide what happens on identity change: refuse it, migrate the values, or document them as abandoned. The document cannot state the contract without this answer.

MIGRATION OF TODAY'S DIY FILES — extensions already shipping (if any) have written their own files under `~/.omp` or `cwd`. Does a future store adopt them, or start clean? The plan is silent. The defensible default is 'start clean, no adoption' — there is no way to know which file belongs to which extension — but the maintainer should say so explicitly in the document rather than leaving it implied, because 'we will migrate later' is the kind of sentence that becomes a breaking change nobody planned.

plan_corrections.claim: The plan frames the design question as a binary: a namespaced key-value store inside the existing layered `Settings`, or a dedicated per-extension store with its own lifecycle.
plan_corrections.correction: It is a ternary, and the third option is the one an author can actually reach today: `pi.appendEntry(<qualified customType>, data)` (signature at `types.ts:1489`) plus a rebuild from `ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()` on `session_start` / `session_branch` / `session_tree`, documented at `docs/extensions.md:699-723` under the heading 'For durable extension state'. It is session-scoped — entries live on a session branch, so nothing survives the session — and it is append-and-replay with latest-match-wins, not a keyed get/set. The design document must rank all three. A document that surveys only the two the plan names will be read as having surveyed the options when it did not, and the first reviewer question will be 'what about the appendEntry pattern that our own docs already recommend?'
plan_corrections.evidence: Read of `docs/extensions.md:699-723` shows the heading, the three numbered steps, and the `session_start` rebuild example using `entry.type === "custom" && entry.customType === "com.example.my-extension.state"`. `git grep -n appendEntry -- packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/` → declared at `types.ts:1489` (ExtensionAPI) and `types.ts:1752` (handler type), implemented at `loader.ts:307-308` delegating to `runner.ts:694`.
